text:
Daemon Hunt started the season in Minnesota and landed in Nashville on a waiver claim on Oct. 24. The timing worked out: the Predators have won seven of the nine games he has played for them, and he has been a steady part of the rotation at about 13 and a half minutes a night.

Don't expect points. He has one assist in 20 games between the two teams and no goals on 1.2 expected, and his ceiling here is a third-pair job, not a power-play one. Evolving-Hockey rated him around replacement level last season in a small sample (398 minutes), with his teams creating very little with him on the ice.

There is one interesting wrinkle. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, over only seven games last season, had him getting to the home-plate area in front of the net at a rate in the 99th percentile for defensemen. If that instinct shows up in Nashville, a first goal is not far off. For now his job is simpler: keep the third pair quiet while the Predators keep winning.
headline: Daemon Hunt finds a home on Nashville's third pair
